title: Service Stability Orchestration Handbook: Incident Scripts, Rotations, and Customer Communications
author: Nina Park
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This handbook captures a single, practical set of patterns for stabilizing services during incidents, aligning on-call rotations, running short restoration sprints, and producing consistent customer-facing communications and postmortems. It is intended for SREs, service owners, on-call engineers, support, and product incident stakeholders.

Scope:
- Applies to service-level incidents that cause user-visible degradation (latency/SLO breaches, increased error rates, throughputs failures) and multi-region failovers.
- NOT intended for purely data-plane debug tasks with zero user impact; those use service-specific debug runbooks.

Quick Reference (two-minute decision ladder):
1) Detect: alert -> confirm signal on at least two data sources (metrics + traces/logs).
2) Contain: apply isolation policy (route blackhole, short-circuit feature flag, scale up staging pool).
3) Stabilize: bring latency/errors back under SLO via fallback or capacity adjustment.
4) Communicate: open bridge, create status entry, notify support/CS.
5) Repair: implement fix or rollback.
6) Review: postmortem within 72 hours (initial blameless summary), detailed RCA within 7 days.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates cross-team work, owns timeline and customer communications.
- Bridge Lead: runs the zoom/bridge, enforces runbook steps and action tracking.
- Triage Engineer: performs root-cause triage, applies containment steps, and executes runbook play.
- Service Owner (PO/Eng): approves rollbacks and change windows; ensures post-incident follow-ups.
- Communications Lead: drafts status page and customer messages; syncs with support/CS.
- SRE On-call: first responder; escalates to SWAT or owners per ladder.

Incident lifecycle: reproducible, numbered steps
1) Detection & Confirmation
   - Validate alert (>=2 signals).
   - Triage: determine impact (users affected, regions, severity).

2) Open Bridge & Assign IC (target: within 5 minutes of confirmation)
   - Use standard bridge URL and run the Bridge Lead script (see below).

3) Contain (immediate actions, 0–15 minutes)
   - Apply targeted mitigations in priority order:
     1. Traffic routing changes (DST route weight adjustments).
     2. Feature-flag critical-path short-circuit.
     3. Autoscale burst policy (if safe).
     4. Throttle low-priority background jobs.
   - Document each action in the bridge notes with actor and timestamp.

4) Stabilize (15–60 minutes)
   - If containment succeeded, move to stabilization verification (slo-check command below).
   - If not, escalate to SWAT (engineers + infra) and consider partial rollback.

5) Repair & Recover (60+ minutes)
   - Decide repair vs rollback. Prefer quick, well-understood rollback when risk of regression is high.
   - When deploying fixes, use canary then graduated rollout.

6) Close & Communicate
   - Post status update (see templates).
   - Schedule post-incident blameless writeup and assign owner.

Bridge Lead Conduct Script (copy-runable):
1) Announce: "This is the service-stability bridge for SERVICE-X. IC is @NAME, Bridge Lead is @NAME."
2) Confirm scope & impact: list affected regions, endpoints, SLO symptoms.
3) Read decision ladder and intended immediate containment action.
4) Call for volunteers for triage/rollback/testing.
5) Record action items into the incident tracker and assign owners.
6) Provide five-minute cadence check-ins; escalate if progress stalls more than 15 minutes.
7) When service stable, confirm with metric checks and runbook verification steps before closing.

Runbook snippets and required commands (example)
- Metric sanity check (CLI):
  $ infra-monitor query --service SERVICE-X --metric p95_latency --since 10m
- Quick rollback (k8s):
  $ kubectl -n svc-x rollout undo deploy/svc-x-api --to-revision=REVERSE_REV
- Canary and promote:
  1) deploy with canary label: kubectl apply -f svc-x-canary.yaml
  2) monitor canary: infra-monitor query --filter canary --metric errors --since 5m

Service Stabilization Checklist (table represented as text)
- Item: Confirmed impacts | Owner: Triager | Accept criteria: >2 signals and customer reports
- Item: Isolation applied | Owner: Triage Engineer | Accept criteria: traffic rerouted or feature-flag toggled
- Item: Latency back under SLO | Owner: IC | Accept criteria: p95 < SLO for 10m rolling window
- Item: Customer comms posted | Owner: Communications Lead | Accept criteria: public status entry + support note

On-call rotation alignment guidance
- Goal: keep primary SRE on 7-day rotation blocks, secondary backup assigned for ramp-down periods.
- Handover checklist for shift changes:
  - Current active incidents and status
  - Outstanding actions and owners with ETA
  - Recent pager noise or unstable services
  - Local changes (deploys, infra maint scheduled)
- Escalation matrix: primary -> secondary -> oncall-lead -> oncall-engineering-manager.

Game day scenarios and objectives
- Scenario A: Regional latency regression under autoscaling threshold. Objective: validate containment via traffic reweight and feature-flag short-circuit.
- Scenario B: Deployment-caused error surge. Objective: practice rapid rollback and canary observation windows.
- Scenario C: Multi-service cascade (DB throttling). Objective: validate cross-team coordination and partial degradation strategies.
- Each game day must produce: runbook gaps list, time-to-stable metric, and one actionable improvement.

Status page and customer communication templates
- Status page short form (initial):
  Title: SERVICE-X Degraded – Increased latency in us-west1
  Started: 2026-02-15T10:08Z
  Impact: Some customers may experience higher latency for API requests.
  Next update: in 15 minutes or when the service transitions states.
- Customer notification (support-first update):
  Subject: Incident affecting SERVICE-X in us-west1 (ongoing)
  Body: "We are investigating increased latency affecting SERVICE-X in the us-west1 region. Our engineering team has opened an incident bridge and applied traffic routing mitigations. We will provide updates every 15 minutes. If you are seeing specific errors, please reply with request IDs or timestamps. We apologize for the disruption."
- Final restoration message (post-stable):
  Subject: SERVICE-X incident resolved – summary and next steps
  Body: "Summary: The incident that began at 2026-02-15T10:08Z causing elevated latency has been resolved at 2026-02-15T11:20Z. Root cause: a deployment introduced an inefficient query under load. Immediate action: rollback to previous revision and increased DB connection limits. Customer impact: increased latency for ~18% of API calls in us-west1 during the window. Follow-up: detailed RCA will be published in the postmortem."

Postmortem & follow-up process (timelines)
- 0–72 hours: blameless incident summary (IC + Bridge Lead), immediate mitigations, and assigned owners for long-term fixes.
- 72 hours – 7 days: full RCA with timeline, contributing factors, and action plan with owners and due dates.
- 7–30 days: implementation of medium-term fixes and verification tests; update postmortem with status.

Postmortem checklist (short)
- Title, severity, timeline of events, human timeline (who did what and when), root cause, contributing factors, mitigations taken, action items (owner, due date), customer impact statement, follow-up verification plan.

Measurement and SLO triggers for this playbook
- SLO breach threshold: p99 errors > 1% sustained for 5 minutes OR p95 latency > SLO + 200ms for 10 minutes.
- Auto-declare incident trigger: sustained alerts from two different observability sources or >=3 customer reports.
- Metrics to capture during incident: p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, queue depth, CPU/GPU utilization, DB connections.

Ownership & escalation contacts (replace in-place with team aliases)
- Primary SRE oncall: @sre-oncall
- Secondary SRE backup: @sre-backup
- Incident Commander rotation lead: @incident-rotation
- Communications lead: @commops

Appendix: sample incident tracker fields (CSV friendly)
- incident_id, service, severity, started_at, resolved_at, ic, bridge_url, actions_taken, customer_impacted, postmortem_link

Appendix: links and references
- Service SLO definitions: /confluence/eng-sre/service-slo-definitions
- Runbook library: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-catalog
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

Notes and governance
- This handbook is a canonical operational pattern; teams may extend with service-specific steps but must map to the decision ladder above.
- Review cadence: annual review and post–major-incident update.
